newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Jan 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Jan 31.

text.p: Japan's leading paperboard maker Japan Paper Industry Co Ltd and Jujo Paper Board Co Ltd have reached an agreement to merge in October to form Japan's second-largest producer of paperboard.
Both are group members of Nippon Paper Industries Co Ltd.
The new company will have total annual sales of more than 100 billion yen and output of around 1.5 million tonnes of paperboard per year.
It will also take over the paperboard marketing operations of Nippon Paper's subsidiary Tohoku Paper Industries Co Ltd, a paperboard company based in Akita in Northen Japan.

Medium-sized Tokyo-based securities company Matsui Securities Co Ltd will cut its brokerage fees by 50 percent on stocks and convertible bonds traded on the over-the-counter (OTC) market from March 3, breaking a uniform pricing pattern among brokerages. Current regulations allow securities companies to freely set the fees they charge for OTC trades, but in practice the companies have adopted standard rates.
U.S. developer American Malls International (AMI) plans to open Japan's largest commercial complex in 2000 a site in Ibaraki Prefecture, north of Tokyo. The mall will cost about 20 billion yen.

Sumitomo Petroleum Development Co Ltd has formed a partnership with French company Elf Aquitaine SA and Malaysia's state-owned Petronas to explore and develop an oil field in Syria. The three have signed an agreement with the Syrian government gioving them the right to drill exploratory wells for $50 million.

Sapporo Breweries Ltd is expecting to see its pre-tax profit fall to 14.5 billion yen in the year to December, 3.5 billion yen below its initial projection, hit by a lower-than-expected sales of beer.
Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd plans to spend about 130 billion yen to triple production capacity of lithium batteries and boost output of other batteries.
